The bridge bank (New Kabul Bank) will be offered for sale in a transparent way, involving a pre-qualification process to ensure that controlling shareholders, beneficial owners, directors and management of intending bidders are fit and proper (which implies, inter alia, that an intending bidder is subject to a high standard of corporate governance, including risk management and internal controls, and that an intending bidder is in a sound financial and risk management state), and that the intending bidder controls adequate resources and has the necessary capacity and capability to ensure the ongoing provision of the relevant salary payments services. The Government will adopt a comprehensive pension reform program before completion of the first review, with Parliamentary passage before completion of the second review. The law will provide for a raising of the pension age for women to 57 at the beginning of 1997, followed by an increase of oneyear every two years until the pension age reaches 62 years. For men, theretirement age will also be raised gradually to 62, beginning with an increase to 61 in 1998. In addition, the minimum service period will be lengthened and the noncontributory service period counted toward retirement will be reduced. On early retirement, following the reform of 1995, further disincentives will be introduced before the completion of the second review; these will include a significant lowering of the pension base for each year of retirement prior to the new statutory retirement age.

In 1996, employment in the general government will be reduced by at least 8 percent relative to 1994. The Government will adopt a medium-term public sector employment program, with implementation beginning in January 1997.

Thus far in 1995-96, cash receipts from privatization have amounted to some Ft 440 billion of which about Ft 342 billion have been transferred to the budget to reduce government debt. Privatization will continue in 1996, albeit on a reduced scale, and we expect that a further amount of Ft 100 billion will be realized; this amount will also be transferred to the central budget to reduce debt. In all, privatization in 1995-96 is expected to yield cash receipts to the APV Rt (the state holding company in charge of privatization) of some Ft 540 billion of which approximately Ft 440 billion will be utilized to reduce government debt. Privatization targets for 1997 will be specified in the fourth quarter of 1996. For small- and mediumsized companies, a first list of companies to be sold was announced in September 1995. A second privatization list will be announced before the first review, with a view to finalizing the sale of most of the enterprises on it by end-year.

The increase in charges to the consumers averages 5 4 percent.

§Regarding the social security system, Parliament is expected to approve a law reforming the system of disability pensions during 1995. Under the new law, eligibility criteria will be based on disability to work rather than on damage to health. Submission of this legislation to Parliament will constitute a structural benchmark for the second review.

Its main objective will be to strengthen the link between individuals' contributions and their entitlement to benefits. In that connection, a focus will be on measures to increase the average retirement age, including, in particular, by raising gradually the statutory retirement age for women and eliminating their right to retire only on the basis of qualifying years. Adoption by the Government of such a comprehensive reform plan will be a structural benchmark for the second review.
